## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Don't merge yet. The new `Cache.set` stores keys without lower-casing them, but `get` always lower-cases. As a result, any key with a capital letter can be stored but never read back. The TTL change and its comment are consistent.

## Critical
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — `set` writes `self._store[key]` with the key exactly as passed, but `get` (line 17) always looks up `key.lower()`. So `c.set("Alpha", 1); c.get("Alpha")` looks up `"alpha"`, finds nothing and returns `None`. Also, `set("Alpha", 1)` followed by `set("alpha", 2)` leaves two separate entries, which the comment at lines 14–15 says must not happen ("every path into _store lower-cases the key first"). Could you change this to `self._store[key.lower()] = (value, time.monotonic() + self._ttl)`, and add a mixed-case key to `test_set_then_get_round_trip`? That test currently only stores `"alpha"`, so it can't catch this. — Any caller that uses a mixed-case key gets silent cache misses, and leftover duplicate entries can't be reached or removed through `get`.

## Strengths
- `test_entries_expire` patches `time.monotonic` on the module that `app/cache.py` uses through `import time`, so the expiry check runs against a fixed clock and gives the same result every run.
- The `DEFAULT_TTL` comment at app/cache.py:7 matches the new value of 300.
